echo_isles_camp_supplies.accept_text: The Tidal Flats - far south of the Landing, where the sand goes grey and the tide leaves the cays standing. The coconut crabs there drag the coral up the beach to line their burrows. They'll fight you for it. They'll lose.

echo_zathra_shards.accept_text: The carvers work the camp fires just north-east of here, and the deeper dens of Zalazane's Hollow - the cave on the island far to the south, across the long bridge. Don't touch the names.

echo_isles_relic_recovery.accept_text: Off the voodoo trolls, the hex trolls and the carvers at the camp fires, right here around the village. The carvers who went south to Zalazane's Hollow carry them too, but you won't need to go that far.

echo_zathra_hexweaver.accept_text: Zalazane's Hollow - the cave on the island to the south, across the long bridge. She keeps a den on its west side, below Zalazane's sanctum.

echo_kesh_pearls.turn_in_text: Perfect. Da tide is already softer. Dese pearls are why da temple's guardians never left. Dey're still lookin' for da last offering. Dere's a drowned warrior down dere who needs rest.

echo_isles_scout_camps.turn_in_text: Dat many?.. Good. Now we know what we're walkin' into. Most people who die out dere die because dey walked in blind. Next job's closer to home, and louder.

echo_muzka_steps.turn_in_text:
You're BRAVE. Say it again, say it where my cousin can hear.

[He stops.]

How many steps were there past the middle one?.. That's what I thought. Nobody ever gets further than that.

echo_dritt_captain.accept_text:
North-east past the troll isle. The flagship's the big one.

The drowned crewmen are still aboard.

echo_tarna_kragg.accept_text: Under the cays on the Tidal Flats. Kill the sand burrowers trailing him and he'll come.

echo_jinzil_beard.description:
One more thing out there, and it's not a thing to me.

The first mate of the Lost Fleet never left his post. Old Barnacle-Beard, the beachcombers called him, back when there were enough of us to call him anything.

He walks the shallows by the wrecks with a lantern in one hand and an axe in the other, looking for the captain's orders.

There are no orders. The captain's been down twenty years. He's walking a dark flat looking for a piece of paper that stopped existing before he did, and he will do it until somebody stops him.

The crabs that infest those flats have gone feral on him. Kill them and he'll come looking for the noise - he can't help it, noise is the job.

Bring me the lantern.

And put the old man down properly. He fights like a man who's already dead, mon, because he is one.
